solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: To break lock, resort to this?

definitions.text: To break lock, resort to this?

indicators.note: a resort breaking a lock means the resort's letters split the lock's letters apart

parts.note: a lock of hair is a tress
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: A burglar unable to pick a lock wonders whether to resort to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: SPA breaking into TRESS builds the word, and someone who breaks a lock to get in is committing the offence.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking a lock to enter someone's property is unlawful entry onto their land or premises.

clue.text: Home for Spartacus and most of the people

indicators.note: most of a phrase means one letter of it is dropped, here a letter from the joined words

parts.note: a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: Spartacus's homeland and most of its population.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims one E from THE RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus, the gladiator who led the slave revolt against Rome, was born in that ancient Balkan region.

clue.text: Top business chief meets top guy at press, the former turning tail

indicators.note: the former, the business chief, turns its tail: its last two letters change places, the C going to the end

parts.note: an exec is an executive, a business chief
the editor, ED, is the top person at a newspaper

explanation.surface: A company boss meets a newspaper editor, then the former turns and runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the former' points back to the business chief, and 'turning tail' swaps the final pair of EXEC to give EXCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To top a figure is to go beyond or surpass it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Seductee shot leader of Union in nuts?

parts.note: a shot is a photograph, a pic

indicators.note: in means the leading letter goes inside the nuts

parts.note: KP is a British brand of peanuts

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word Union

explanation.surface: Someone seduced was shot by a trade-union leader who was nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: KP Nuts are a familiar British snack brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone picked up in a bar for a casual encounter is the person who has been seduced.

clue.text: Fat marshals count on author of 8 books?

indicators.note: to marshal is to gather and hold together, so the fat holds the count inside it

parts.note: suet is hard animal fat
Graf is the German title for a count

explanation.surface: An overweight official lines people up for a tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is the entry at 8-down: her mystery novels run A Is for Alibi, B Is for Burglar and onward through the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The American crime novelist wrote a series of mysteries titled by successive letters, A to Y.

clue.text: Joe and I getting worried … something following me around tree

indicators.note: around means the note's letters go around the rest

parts.note: in the sol-fa scale (doh, ray, me, fah) the note after me is fa

indicators.note: worried here means agitated, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Joe and I fret as something follows me round a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting worried' rearranges JOEI to EIJO, which sits inside FA.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a South American evergreen shrub or small tree grown for its green fruit.

clue.text: Introduce Old Vic landlord to European in place of proof

indicators.note: introduce means the landlord is put inside the other piece

parts.note: vice, as in vice-captain, means in place of
Den Watts was the original landlord of the Queen Vic pub in EastEnders

explanation.surface: Bringing the Old Vic's landlord in to replace a European.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Vic is a London theatre, but here it is the Queen Vic, the pub in the BBC soap EastEnders, whose first landlord was Den.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is the facts or testimony that establish a case, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Opinion formed by Tony Hall, say, on people working in project

indicators.note: in means the two pieces go inside the word for project

parts.note: to project is to jut out

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: Tony Hall was Director-General of the BBC, a DG
working people are men, as in workmen

explanation.surface: A view formed by the BBC's Tony Hall about staff on a project.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Hall was the BBC's Director-General from 2013 to 2020.
explanation.definitionFit: A judgment is a considered view or assessment, so it is an opinion.

clue.text: Keeping record, heads of Austria and Hungary make good spellers?

indicators.note: keeping means the two heads hold the record between them
heads of means the first letters of the words Austria and Hungary

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
to abet is to help a deed succeed, taken here as making it good

explanation.surface: Austrian and Hungarian leaders, holding a record, produce fine spellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spellers' are things that spell words, the letters, and the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The set of letters, from A to Z, is what all written words are spelt with.

clue.text: Paradoxically, one caught in the firing line with right to left shot?

indicators.note: to left means the right piece goes at the far left, the front

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: paradoxically flags the reverse of what is said: the firing line is not caught in, the caught piece holds the line
in signals the insertion, though the paradox turns it round

parts.note: the oche is the line darts players throw from

explanation.surface: A paradox: one caught in the firing line, a shot from right to left.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly, 'caught in the firing line' puts CT inside OCHE; 'Paradoxically' flips it, putting OCHE inside CT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullet that rebounds off a surface is a deflected shot that can hit someone not aimed at.

clue.text: Patting baby's back, parent may get this close?

definitions.text: Patting baby's back, parent may get this
definitions.meaning: burping a baby brings up trapped air, so the parent gets it rising
to close a meeting or business is to end it, a phrasal verb

explanation.surface: A parent pats a baby's back and gets something close.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring an event to its end is to finish or conclude it, a phrasal verb sense.

clue.text: With Her Majesty intervening, is applauding Boris's retreat

indicators.note: intervening means coming between, so the royal abbreviation goes inside

parts.note: someone who is applauding cheers
QU is an abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: With the Queen present, someone applauds Boris Johnson's getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prime Minister's official country house in Buckinghamshire; Boris Johnson was PM when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: The Buckinghamshire country house is the official weekend residence of the British Prime Minister.

clue.text: Perhaps Helena's contrary object of desire — or Lysander's?

parts.note: a woman's possession, Helena's for one, is hers, the possessive her

indicators.note: contrary means the word for object of desire is turned backwards

parts.note: an aim is an object one desires

explanation.surface: A question from A Midsummer Night's Dream: whose object of desire is she?
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream Helena loves Demetrius, while Lysander loves her friend; the 'or' sets up Lysander's object of desire as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's comedy the young woman who elopes with Lysander is the girl he loves.

clue.text: 'Just a little fling', disgusted, dishabillé guide admitted

indicators.note: admitted means the undressed guide is let inside

parts.note: to flounce is to fling oneself off in disgust

indicators.note: dishabillé means undressed, so the guide loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: A disgusted, half-dressed guide admits it was 'just a little fling'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishabillé' strips GUIDE to UID, which goes into FLOUNCE.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a small liquid measure, a fraction of a pint, so a tiny amount.

clue.text: Being drunk and disorderly, say, left in charge in here?

indicators.note: the second in means the two short pieces go inside the offence

parts.note: being drunk and disorderly is an example of a criminal offence

explanation.surface: Is being drunk and disorderly something you get for leaving charge of yourself here?
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the shop where the drink that leads to that offence is bought.
explanation.definitionFit: A British shop licensed to sell alcohol for drinking elsewhere is a place to buy drink.

clue.text: Impeccable hotel supported by none of Trump's money

indicators.note: in a down clue supported by means the hotel sits above the rest

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
O is zero, none
the cent is a unit of US currency, Trump's money

explanation.surface: A flawless hotel bankrolled with none of Trump's cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone blameless or without fault is without sin or guilt, a synonym.

clue.text: Fleeing university, heading for great time? That will enthral one in five

indicators.note: in means the built piece goes inside the word five
to enthral is to hold captive, so the three letters hold the one inside
heading for means the first letter of the word great

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing university to have a great time, enthralling one in five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will enthral' puts I into UGT to make UGIT, and 'in' places that inside FIVE; 'That' points back to UGT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person on the run from capture is one escaping, an adjectival sense of running away.

clue.text: It's #26-1 without sections

parts.note: # means number: letter number 26 of the alphabet is Z
the figure 1 written as a word is one
the minus sign is read as less

explanation.surface: It looks like a cross-reference to entries 26 and 1, with no sections.
explanation.walkthrough: The # and hyphen look like a pointer to other entries, but # is number: the 26th letter, then ONE, then the minus sign read as LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not divided into areas or regions has no zones at all.

clue.text: Retiring President about to regret poisoning agent

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the whole is read backwards
about means the president's letters go around the rest

parts.note: Richard Nixon was a US President
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A retiring president is about to regret a poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TORUE inside NIXON as NIXOTORUEN; 'Retiring' reverses all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a toxin that attacks the nervous system, a substance that poisons nerves.

clue.text: Offer to lag low-down part of machine

indicators.note: lagging wraps a pipe, so the offer is wrapped around the low-down

parts.note: a bid is an offer
gen is slang for information, the low-down

explanation.surface: A proposal to insulate the lowest part of a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low-down' looks like the definition's position in an engine; it is the slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: In an engine it is the larger end of the connecting rod, gripping the crankshaft.

clue.text: Steal look over widening moor

indicators.note: widening means the word for moor is stretched open to fit the instruction inside

parts.note: to moor a boat is to tie it up
PTO, please turn over, tells a reader to look over the page

explanation.surface: Taking a look over a broadening moor.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal along is to move quietly and stealthily, as on the balls of one's feet.

clue.text: Bird taking flight, setter and solver record it

indicators.note: taking flight means the letters fly off and land in a new order

parts.note: the setter and the solver together are we
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A bird takes off as the setter and solver capture it on record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking flight' shuffles WEEP to PEEW, and IT follows as written.
explanation.definitionFit: It is another name for the lapwing, named after its call.

clue.text: Musical, as it happens, has a band of gold

indicators.note: having a band of gold means the gold letters wrap round the rest

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a live broadcast goes out as it happens

explanation.surface: A live show wearing a gold band.
explanation.definitionFit: Lionel Bart's stage show is based on Dickens's novel about a workhouse orphan.

clue.text: In which cases start to involve detectives?

definitions.text: In which cases start to involve detectives?

indicators.note: to case is to enclose, so the home letters enclose the rest

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the word involve

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detectives

explanation.surface: In which cases do detectives start to get involved?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a killing is the kind of case that brings detectives in.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlawful killing is the crime detectives are always called to investigate.

clue.text: Performer's source of wealth divides them

definitions.note: the 's is short for is, linking the performer to the wordplay

indicators.note: to divide is to come between, so the source of wealth splits the other piece

parts.note: 'em is a casual short form of them
a mine is a source of wealth

explanation.surface: A performer's fortune is splitting the group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Detroit rapper Marshall Mathers is a famous stage act.

clue.text: Not yet a couple, love misplaced, getting pulled?

indicators.note: misplaced means the letter is put in a different spot within the phrase

parts.note: a couple is two, so not yet a couple is under two
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Not yet a couple, the love misplaced, someone is getting pulled in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misplaced' shifts the O of UNDER TWO one place to make UNDER TOW; 'getting pulled' evokes the slang sense of being chatted up.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel being towed by another is being drawn along behind it.

clue.text: Pretty little 13-19-year-olds on verge of twenty

parts.note: those aged thirteen to nineteen are teens

indicators.note: on the verge of means the edge, here the last letter of the word twenty

explanation.surface: Pretty young teenagers on the verge of turning twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretty means rather here, and something rather small is tiny.

clue.text: Idler no longer running course for PCs

parts.note: something no longer running, an engine say, is dead
a beat is the route a police constable patrols

explanation.surface: A lazy man who stopped jogging on the police's route.
explanation.walkthrough: PCs here are police constables, not computers.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout who avoids work is a lazy, feckless sort of person.
